originalTitle: HoverAir’s transforming modular drone has already been halted in the US
summary: I am so sorry, fellow US gadget fans: the FCC's drone ban appears to have struck again. The HoverAir Versa - a baby steadycam with snap-on propeller wings that transform it into a drone - has already stopped taking US orders just three days after its Indiegogo debut, and may be forced to abandon shipping […]
content: I am so sorry, fellow US gadget fans: the FCC’s drone ban appears to have struck again. The HoverAir Versa — a baby steadycam with snap-on propeller wings that transform it into a drone — has already stopped taking US orders just three days after its Indiegogo debut, and may be forced to abandon shipping plans in the US. HoverAir is now telling backers it’s only shipping its camera to the US, not the piece that turns it into a drone, “due to a few remaining logistics updates with the Flight Kit.” But those “logistics” may actually be a euphemism for “we’ve been banned by the federal government.” The FCC’s database no longer has an entry for the HoverAir Versa at all, suggesting that its authorization grant has been pulled. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/chrome_LOHM8EWKql.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] On Wednesday, I told you how giving a camera wings probably wasn’t a good enough loophole to keep the FCC from feeling tricked. Even though the HoverAir Versa did make it through the FCC on August 9th, we confirmed, that approval was for a camera, not a drone. The Chinese company, Zero Zero Robotics, told the FCC’s agent the camera shouldn’t be blocked because Zero Zero isn’t on the FCC’s Covered List for cameras — which is true. But all companies are automatically on the FCC’s covered list for drones and critical drone components, and the FCC explicitly defines cameras as one of those components. [Image: Early buyers may need refunds. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/chrome_0z9pEtE6iT.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] If HoverAir’s camera authorization is now rejected, it won’t just be the “Flight Kit” accessory that it can’t import, market, or sell in the United States. The camera portion won’t be legal, either, as it needs FCC authorization too. Currently, HoverAir’s Indiegogo page no longer shows the “Flight Kit” as a selectable option to people browsing from the US, but it does still market it, and backers can order the camera portion. When I use a VPN to change my internet address to Canada, combos that include the Flight Kit suddenly appear. That won’t help US residents buy one, though. In the Indiegogo comments section, one backer who already ordered the camera wrote: “When looking at my pledge, it shows that they can’t ship to my address.” [Image: These are the only options now available to backers in the US, and even they may disappear. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/chrome_SnXkyebCYe.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] HoverAir did not immediately respond to a request for comment. We’ve asked the company whether it will commit to refunds more quickly this time around — when the brand failed to obtain certification for the waterproof HoverAir Aqua last December, it spent months telling backers it would ship as soon as possible rather than revealing the truth. I tried to speak to the FCC about what’s going on, but once again, an agency spokesperson refused to go on the record.
chineseTitle: HoverAir 的模块化无人机转型已在美国叫停
chineseSummary: 我很抱歉，美国电子产品迷们：联邦通信委员会的无人机禁令似乎再次袭来。 HoverAir Versa——一款带有卡扣式螺旋桨翼的小型稳定摄像机，可以将其转变为无人机——在 Indiegogo 首次亮相三天后就已经停止接受美国订单，并且可能被迫放弃发货 [...]
chineseContent: 我很抱歉，美国电子产品迷们：联邦通信委员会的无人机禁令似乎再次袭来。 HoverAir Versa——一款带有卡扣式螺旋桨翼的小型稳定摄像机，可将其转变为无人机——在 Indiegogo 首次亮相三天后就已经停止接受美国订单，并且可能被迫放弃在美国的发货计划。 HoverAir 现在告诉支持者，它只将其相机运送到美国，而不是将其变成无人机的部件，“因为飞行套件还剩下一些物流更新。”但这些“后勤”实际上可能是“我们已被联邦政府禁止”的委婉说法。 FCC 的数据库中根本不再有 HoverAir Versa 的条目，这表明其授权已被撤回。 [图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/chrome_LOHM8EWKql.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] 周三，我告诉过你，给相机机翼可能不足以让 FCC 感到被欺骗。尽管 HoverAir Versa 确实于 8 月 9 日通过了 FCC，但我们确认，该批准是针对相机，而不是无人机。中国公司“零零机器人”告诉 FCC 的工作人员，不应封锁该摄像头，因为“零零”并不在 FCC 的摄像头覆盖列表中——这是事实。但所有公司都会自动列入 FCC 的无人机和关键无人机组件清单，并且 FCC 明确将摄像头定义为这些组件之一。 [图片：早期买家可能需要退款。 https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/chrome_0z9pEtE6iT.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]如果HoverAir的相机授权现在被拒绝，那么它就不仅仅是“飞行套件”配件无法在美国进口、营销或销售。相机部分也不合法
